'''Giordano''': {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Joe Lieberman]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Joe Lieberman]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsCT}} The '''2000 United States Senate election in Connecticut''' took place on November 7, 2000. Democratic incumbent [[Joe Lieberman]], who was also the Democratic nominee for vice president in the [[2000 United States presidential election|concurrent presidential election]], was re-elected to a third term in a landslide over [[Waterbury, Connecticut|Waterbury]] mayor [[Philip Giordano|Phil Giordano]]. == Background == While running for re-election to the Senate, Lieberman was also the Democratic nominee for [[Vice President of the United States|vice president]] in the [[2000 United States presidential election|concurrent presidential election]], as the chosen running mate of presidential nominee [[Al Gore]]. Had the Gore-Lieberman ticket won, Lieberman would have resigned his Senate seat (regardless of the result of this election) prior to becoming vice president. The Senate vacancy would have been filled through a 2002 special election, and Republican governor [[John G. Rowland]] would have appointed an interim replacement to serve until such election.{{Cite web |url=https://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/courant/access/57664553.html?dids=57664553:57664553&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Aug+08%2C+2000&author=MATTHEW+KAUFFMAN+And+CARRIE+BUDOFF%3B+Courant+Staff+Writers%3B+Courant+Staff+Writer+Lyn+Bixby+contributed+to+this+story%2C+which+also+includes+a+wire+service+report.&pub=Hartford+Courant&desc=SENATOR+TO+CONTINUE+RE-ELECTION+EFFORTS%2C+TOO+LAW+PERMITS+STATEWIDE+AND+NATIONWIDE+RUNS%3B+JOSEPH+LIEBERMAN%3A+THE+HISTORIC+CHOICE+Series%3A+VOTE+2000&pqatl=google |title = Proquest - Courant.com |access-date=2017-07-07 |archive-date=2012-11-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105092358/http://pqasb.pqarchiver.com/courant/access/57664553.html?dids=57664553:57664553&FMT=ABS&FMTS=ABS:FT&type=current&date=Aug+08,+2000&author=MATTHEW+KAUFFMAN+And+CARRIE+BUDOFF%3B+Courant+Staff+Writers%3B+Courant+Staff+Writer+Lyn+Bixby+contributed+to+this+story,+which+also+includes+a+wire+service+report.&pub=Hartford+Courant&desc=SENATOR+TO+CONTINUE+RE-ELECTION+EFFORTS,+TOO+LAW+PERMITS+STATEWIDE+AND+NATIONWIDE+RUNS%3B+JOSEPH+LIEBERMAN:+THE+HISTORIC+CHOICE+Series:+VOTE+2000&pqatl=google |url-status=dead }} ==General election== ===Candidates=== *[[Joe Lieberman]], incumbent U.S. senator since 1989 (Democratic) *[[Philip Giordano]], [[Waterbury, Connecticut|Waterbury]] mayor and former [[Connecticut House of Representatives|state representative]] (Republican) *Wildey J. Bush]], Lieberman returned to the Senate and remained there until his retirement in 2013. This was the last Senate election in which Lieberman formally ran as the Democratic nominee. In [[2006 United States Senate election in Connecticut|2006]], he ran on the [[Connecticut for Lieberman]] ticket following his loss in the Democratic Party primary.
